history.summary: NON-TEMPLE: KEEP-OR-DROP DECISION NEEDED — Vandiyur Mariamman Teppakulam is a large sacred temple TANK (water reservoir), not a temple building, like seq 2086 (Shyam Kund, sacred tank precedent). Built in 1645 by King Thirumalai Nayak, it is among the largest temple tanks in Tamil Nadu — about 16 acres, roughly 305 m x 290 m (1000 ft x 950 ft), with granite stepped walkways on all four sides and the Maiya Mandapam (central mandapam) holding a Vinayakar temple and garden in the middle. Legend: the pit formed when soil was dug to make bricks for Thirumalai Nayakkar Mahal (some sources say for the Meenakshi Amman Temple instead — flag variation). The tank is fed from the Vaigai River through underground channels. It is the venue of the annual float festival (Teppam) in January-February, when the idols of Meenakshi and Sundareshwarar are carried around the water on decorated floats. A separate Vandiyur Mariamman Temple (Mariamman as goddess of rain) stands near the tank. About 5 km east of the Meenakshi Amman Temple in Madurai.

name: Vandiyur Mariamman Teppakulam
town_description: Madurai is the temple city of Tamil Nadu in Madurai district on the Vaigai River, famous for the Meenakshi Amman Temple. The Teppakulam lies in the Vandiyur area about 5 km east of the Meenakshi temple.
tradition: Hinduism (Shaktism — sacred temple tank associated with Mariamman and Meenakshi Amman)

travel.road: About 5 km east of the Meenakshi Amman Temple; accessible by auto, car and city buses via Teppakulam West Street, Meenakshi Nagar.
